inputs.name: seed

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

facts.text: Tracking-Flat-G1-v0 is registered with entry point isaaclab.envs:ManagerBasedRLEnv, env_cfg_entry_point flat_env_cfg.G1FlatEnvCfg and rsl_rl_cfg_entry_point G1FlatPPORunnerCfg, with the environment checker disabled
The repository targets Isaac Sim 4.5.0, Isaac Lab 2.1.0, Python 3.10 and Linux
G1FlatEnvCfg subclasses TrackingEnvCfg and sets the G1 cylinder robot, the G1 joint action scale, the torso_link motion anchor and 14 tracked body names from pelvis to the wrists and ankles
TrackingEnvCfg is a ManagerBasedRLEnvCfg that groups the scene, observations, actions, commands, rewards, terminations, events and curriculum configuration
The environment uses decimation 4 over a 0.005 s simulation step and an episode length of 10.0 s, so one control step is 0.02 s and the time-out is 500 control steps
The sole action term is a joint-position action over every joint of the robot with the default joint positions as offset
G1_ACTION_SCALE maps every actuator joint expression to 0.25 * effort_limit_sim / stiffness

The policy observation group concatenates command, motion anchor position, motion anchor orientation, base linear velocity, base angular velocity, joint position, joint velocity and the last action, in that order, with corruption enabled
The motion command is the concatenation of the reference joint positions and joint velocities loaded from the motion file
MotionLoader asserts that the motion file exists and loads fps, joint_pos, joint_vel and body pose, quaternion and velocity arrays from a numpy NPZ file
MotionCommandCfg.motion_file is MISSING, so a reset cannot run until a motion file is supplied to the command term by the caller

The termination terms cut an episode when the anchor-z error exceeds 0.25, the projected-gravity error of the anchor exceeds 0.8, or a tracked end-effector body's z error exceeds 0.25, and time_out ends it at the episode length
The command configuration sets the reset pose ranges, the velocity range and a joint position range of -0.1 to 0.1
The robot description is not part of the clone: the README downloads unitree_description.tar.gz from GCS into the package assets directory before the G1 URDF can be spawned
Reference motions are stored in and loaded from the WandB registry, and the reference motion must be retargeted to the robot and use generalized coordinates
The training script creates the environment with gym.make(task, cfg=env_cfg), so the registered environment is driven through the Gymnasium make/step/reset interface

determinism.notes: the upstream environment draws its initial pose, velocity and joint-position randomization from the seeded simulator and the motion command term, and the motion file is fixed, so one seed and one action sequence are intended to repeat a trajectory on the same engine; this package's fake draws its reset state from Python's random.Random, so the same seed gives a different trajectory on the fake and upstream, and no upstream run was made

gaps: the deployed model is Isaac Sim/PhysX rigid-body dynamics with contacts (F1), but the fake backend is a pure Python analytic stand-in: it models no contacts, actuator forces, joint limits, sensors or contact or observation noise, and its numeric constants are placeholders, not the model's

one cap.world.step tick is one control step of 20 ms (the configuration's decimation 4 over the 0.005 s physics step); the physics step itself is 5 ms, and a client that needs it reads this note rather than timestep_ms, which names the step the bridge counts

the fake does not load the G1 URDF (downloaded from GCS, README.md:46-55) or a motion NPZ (assigned to the command term by the caller, commands.py:30-42 and 357-361): its 29-element action vector and 160-element flat observation are placeholder sizes, and the observation terms are zeros and an identity orientation rather than the configured MDP terms

the upstream policy observation group has eight terms (tracking_env_cfg.py:113-133) whose command width comes from the motion NPZ; the fake returns one flat float vector, while the upstream environment returns its observation groups as tensors

the fake models no reward term, no termination event and no time_out DoneTerm: it always returns a zero reward and terminated=False, and truncates at 500 control steps only because that follows from episode_length_s 10.0 and the 0.02 s control step

the action space is unbounded in this package because the clone states no action bound (the action scale of g1.py:184-195 maps a unitless action to a joint target); the fake applies a placeholder gain instead of that scale and enforces the array length only
no physical robot is modelled and nothing was validated against hardware; the environment is trained in simulation and deployment is delegated to a separate repository (README.md:23-24)
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by the declared step only
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state or set_state
the upstream environment was never constructed here (Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab are absent) and the fake was never compared with an upstream run

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
